To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) WFST-based decoding methods are the most promising ones, (2) dynamic expansion search is not a viable solution for large vocabulary tasks, (3) stack decoding can be very efficient but it is not yet fully optimized, (4) heuristic search space reduction methods should be carefully evaluated and (5) there is still a need for a new decoding paradigm.
the WFST decoding method is the most accurate, the asynchronous stack decoding the fastest and the dynamic-expansion search is in between.

1) WFSTs are the most efficient way to represent the search space for LVCSR, 2) dynamic expansion of the search space is a must for LVCSR and 3) the asynchronous search is the most efficient way for decoding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of decoding methods for LVCSR, with a focus on their ability to handle large search spaces and to integrate linguistic and acoustic constraints.
the design and implementation of a new decoding architecture that is based on the combination of a static network and a dynamic search.
the development of efficient algorithms and architectures for large vocabulary speech recognition, with particular emphasis on the integration of linguistic constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best approach to LVCSR is a combination of the three main classes of decoding algorithms, i.e., the WFST, the dynamic-expansion search, and the stack decoding.
the choice of the most appropriate method is problem dependent, and depends on the trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness, and on the available resources.
there is not yet a clear-cut winner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WFST-based decoding methods have the best performance and are most likely to be adopted in commercial systems.
WFST-based methods provide an elegant solution for the static network expansion problem.
the use of WFST is the most promising approach for the design of LVCSR decoding systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WFST-based decoding is currently the best approach for LVCSR.
the search space representation is an essential component for the design of a LVCSR system.
there is no single optimal solution for the design of the LVCSR decoder.
